actions.name: Write meeting notes
actions.prompt:
Write well-structured and readable meeting notes based on what I said, heard, and wrote.
The goal is to make it easy for me to quickly recall what was discussed, decided, and planned during the meeting.

Follow these formatting and writing rules carefully:

### Structure
Organize the notes in the following order (omit any section if not relevant):
1. Meeting Overview
 - Briefly summarize the purpose and key context of the meeting in 2–3 sentences.
 - Include participants, date, and duration.
 - Add 2–3 hashtags that serve as quick reminders of the main topics.
2. Key Discussion Points
 - Bullet list of the main topics covered and important ideas shared.
3. Decisions Made
 - Bullet list of clear outcomes, agreements, or conclusions reached.
4. Action Items
 - Present as a Markdown table with the following columns:
 - Task: What needs to be done (concise and actionable)
 - Owner: Who is responsible (use real names)
 - Due / Timeline: If mentioned, include it; otherwise, leave blank.
5. Key Sections
 - Divide the meeting into logical sections based on topic or flow.
 - For each section, include a short, descriptive title and the timestamp (start time in minutes or seconds) so I can easily locate it when listening back to the audio.
6. Additional Context
 - Optional section for any relevant context, insights, or remarks not fitting above sections.

### Writing Style
 - Use a clear, concise, and professional tone.
 - Do not include a title.
 - Structure the notes using proper heading levels, bullet points, and formatting.
 - Use level-2 headings (##) for each main section, and level-3 headings (###) for sub sections.
 - Add a horizontal divider (---) after each section.
 - Avoid repetition, filler, or unnecessary phrasing.
 - If my manual notes contradict the transcript, prioritize my manual notes.

actions.name: Extract action items
actions.prompt:
Analyze the entire meeting transcript and extract all unfinished or pending action items discussed during the conversation.
Identify any task, follow-up, or responsibility that was mentioned but not yet completed. Focus only on actionable items — things someone needs to do after the meeting.

### Output Format:
Return the results as a markdown table format using the following columns for each action item:

 - Task: <concise, action-oriented summary of what needs to be done, including a timestamp at the end if applicable>
 - Assignee: <person responsible or "Not specified">
 - Due: <deadline or "Not mentioned">

List each action item as a separate block following this structure.

### Guidelines:
 • Exclude completed or historical tasks.
 • Combine duplicate or overlapping items into one concise entry.
 • Keep each task actionable and specific.

actions.name: Generate outline
actions.prompt:
Create a simple, chronological outline of everything discussed in the meeting.

### Format
 - A nested bullet list in the order topics came up.
 - Top-level bullets: topics, each starting with the timestamp [mm:ss] where it began.
 - Sub-bullets: the key points, questions, and answers within that topic — short phrases, not full sentences.
 - Do not add a title, summary, or conclusions — only the outline.
